findings.issue: The branch adds expansive depth mode, completed-run extension (completed-continue via --extend) and custom review dimensions, edits the convergence-mode docs, and documents them in the packet SKILL.md files and command flag tables, but the hub's only authored mode vocabulary carries no feature term. The branch's only change to this file is the version bump 2.0.2.0 -> 2.1.6.0. A probe that names a feature without also naming its mode takes the defer outcome (evidence), so the hub asks the operator to disambiguate a request it could serve. Stage two (ROUTER.md INTENT_SIGNALS) carries the same 12/17 terms with no feature term, so both stages agree on the wrong vocabulary, and every router gate stays green because none of them scores feature phrases. Fix: author feature terms in research-aliases and review-aliases (expansive depth, depth mode, review sub-targets, completed-continue, extend a research run, custom dimensions), mirror them in ROUTER.md INTENT_SIGNALS, and regenerate. Do not add the packet's generic phrases such as 'review code quality': the packet's own When NOT to Use sends those to sk-code, and the S8 lens requires that a phrase fix not steal another skill's prompts.

findings.issue: The hub's advisor-facing vocabulary carries no term for the branch's new features. The keywords here and graph-metadata.json's intent_signals - the array the advisor actually scores, per skill_advisor.py's _extend_signal_map call - stop at the mode names, so a request that names a feature without its mode is not scored to the hub. 'Review the payments module in expansive depth mode with a frontier of review sub-targets' ranks sk-code first with system-deep-loop absent from the ranking (evidence), 'Review the release against custom dimensions beyond the four canonical ones' ranks sk-code first, and 'Investigate the retry policy in expansive depth mode...' returns no recommendation at all. Fix: add the feature terms to graph-metadata.json intent_signals, mirror them in this keywords list, then rebuild the advisor graph so the projected triggers carry them; the same terms must land in hub-router.json and ROUTER.md for the compiled route.

findings.issue: The --depth-mode row was rewritten on this branch (commit 8fda03e7135 introduced it) but kept a pilot-testing chore in shipped command text: '(record the pilot range SHA; ...)'. The command standard's Step 8 forbids development notes in the command body, the phrase names no flag, config field or workflow step, and a repository-wide search finds it in no skill doc or playbook, so an executor that follows it has to invent a write. Fix: drop the chore and keep the pruning behavior it was attached to.

The checker already exempts the same class for .skilled/skills/.state/ and the deep-loop sqlite stores, but not the spec-kit telemetry store, so speckit-resume.yaml:104's reference fails pre-flight even though the command handles a missing pointer. Fix: extend the runtime-generated skip list.
